voyage.name: Al Ahmadiya School and Heritage House
voyage.content: Built in 1912, Al Ahmadiya School was Dubai's first school and has now been nicely restored. It would be a stretch to call the exhibits of old reed pens and diplomas fascinating, but they've tried pretty hard, and if nothing else, the air-con and clean toilets may come in handy. The attached heritage house is a traditional Emirati-style home built in the 1890s.

voyage.name: Deira Clocktower
voyage.address: Abu Baker Al Siddiqe Rd 110 crossing Al Maktoum Rd 105
voyage.content: A landmark of Deira and important as a monument built before the independence of UAE.

voyage.name: Dhow Wharfage
voyage.address: Baniyas Rd, Rigga Al Buteen community 125
voyage.content: The dhows ply the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean, transporting goods between south and south-west Asia and east Africa.

voyage.name: Mamzar Park
voyage.address: 104 Al Khaleej Rd, Al Mamzar community
voyage.content: You can swim at Al Mamzar Beach or stroll in the park. Though less popular than other Dubai parks, it has its share of Dubai's greenery. Monday & Wednesday for women only.

voyage.name: Dubai Municipality Museum
voyage.hours: Sun–Thu 9AM–3PM, closed and Fri and Sat
voyage.address: Old Baladiya St crossing Al Souk Al Kabeer St, Al Buteen community

voyage.name: Women's Museum
voyage.address: 28 St, Al Dhagaya community, P.O. Box 1086
voyage.content: Highlight the contribution of women to UAE's economy, culture and politic for the independence in the 1960s and since. Life of great women and daily life of Emirati people. An exhibit is also dedicated to the famous Emirati female poet Ousha bint Khalifa Suwidi.

voyage.name: Naif Police Museum
voyage.hours: Sun–Thu 8AM–2PM, closed on Fri and Saturday.
voyage.address: 106 Naif Rd crossing 9A St, Naif community

voyage.name: Gold Price Checking - Dubai Souq
voyage.price: Prices vary based on market rate
voyage.content: Before purchasing gold in Dubai’s famous Gold Souk, it's always best to check the current live gold prices. Gold prices fluctuate daily due to global market trends. Visit [GoldRateUAE](https://goldrateuae.ae/) to get the latest price updates. Prices here are available for various gold types including 22K, 24K, and 18K gold.

voyage.name: Cinecity - Al Ghurair Centre
voyage.address: Al Ghurair City, Al Riqqah St
voyage.content: The largest cinema chain in the Middle East. It is a part of Novo Cinemas group. This 8-screen cinema complex including 14 anchor stores has 2 levels.

voyage.name: VOX Deira City Centre
voyage.content: VOX has 11 screens with various types of experiences for movie lovers. The immersive experience of DepthQ 3D technology, fully reclining seats, VIP seats, 20-m screens and brightest and clearest pictures is their latest addition.

voyage.name: Dubai Creek Golf & Yacht Club
voyage.address: Radisson Blu Hotel, Dubai Deira Creek, Bani Yas Rd, 476
voyage.content: This leisure hub is an ideal destination for golfers. It provides wide-ranging set of services, floodlit par-3 course, modern golf academies and driving ranges. Visitors can enjoy a challenging game of golf, hire a private boat to enjoy the calm waters or take a swim.

voyage.name: Dinner Dhow Cruises
voyage.hours: tour start every hour, from 8:30PM onwards
voyage.address: Pier 1 in Dhow Wharfage, Baniyas Rd, Rigga Al Buteen community
voyage.content: A 2-hour dhow cruise tour on a "5-star" dhow, along Dubai Creek with commentary in English.

voyage.name: Jungle Bay Waterpark
voyage.address: Le Meridien Mina Seyahi Beach Resort & Marina
voyage.content: Brand new waterpark, as of April 2021.

voyage.name: City Centre Deira
voyage.address: Banyias Rd, Alittihad Rd, Port Saeed community
voyage.content: By far the most popular mall in Dubai. Debenhams, Virgin Megastore, Zara and other international high street brands. A multiplex cinema, and many restaurants and cafes. Also has a large "Arabian Treasures" souvenir and traditional textiles area. A new extension includes many more high-end boutiques and upmarket mall restaurants. A big Carrefour hypermarket sells just about everything and is nearly always very busy. T

voyage.name: Gold Souk
voyage.address: 106 Sikkat Al Khail Rd, Al Ras community
voyage.content: Not a mall, but a historic market that has been a part of Dubai since the origin of Dubai itself. Located at the mouth of the creek, it dazzles people by selling gold in large quantities and with little visible security. A must visit for shoppers and sightseers. Most of the gold is 22ct quality and quite expensive - although even here the shopkeepers are prepared to bargain - and the craftsmanship can be remarkably d

voyage.name: Spice Souk
voyage.content: Also not a mall, but a historic market that has been a part of Dubai since the city's origin. Located at the mouth of the creek, it is not far from the Gold Souk, but declined a bit in the 2010s as supermarkets take over the spice trade. If you're shopping for spices, odds are you'll get better prices and quality with much less hassle at Carrefour. Both the Spice Souk and the Gold Souq are a rather hot and sweaty exp

voyage.name: Fish Market
voyage.address: Al Mina Rd crossing Baniyas Rd, Deira Corniche
voyage.content: A modern covered market where they sell various kind of fish and seafood, as well as fruits, vegetables, dates (and some kitchen utensils). Its colorful variety of fresh fish is a remarkable sight and fishermen offer their tasty goods for sale and scatter ice to protect seafood from scorching hot weather.

voyage.name: Traditional Souq
voyage.hours: 9AM–10PM daily, but most shop are closed on Fri morning
voyage.content: Souk with air-conditioning, nice decoration and good infrastructure, let say almost a souk almost a mall. 100 shops and 6,100 square-meters. Khalid Huriah Public Restaurant in the middle.

voyage.name: Al Romaizan
voyage.address: Gold Land Bldg, 2nd Floor Office No:205-206, Gold Souq Deira
voyage.content: Al Romaizan is one of the leading gold and jewellery companies in the GCC. Headquartered in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

voyage.name: Bhatkal Restaurant
voyage.content: An Indian restaurant

voyage.name: Al Bait ALqadeem Restaurant and Cafe
voyage.content: A traditional restaurant

voyage.name: Al-Karmel Somali Restaurant
voyage.content: East African cuisine

voyage.name: Avon Restaurant
voyage.content: An Indian Restaurant

voyage.name: Africana Home Restaurant Nakheel Deira Park
voyage.address: 1820, Lootah Building Behind Golden Square Hotel Street 118

voyage.name: Al Dawaar Revolving Restaurant
voyage.price: Lunch: 185 dirhams per person, dinner: 235 dirhams per person
voyage.content: Serving an assortment of cuisines, the highlight of this beautiful restaurant is that it revolves, giving a nice tour of the city.

voyage.name: Al Fanar Restaurant & Cafe
voyage.address: Canal Walk, Dubai Festival City Mall
voyage.content: Authentic Emirati cuisine, in the ambience of Dubai recreated from the 1960s.

voyage.name: Kiku
voyage.content: Japanese cuisine. Very high quality and very popular.

voyage.name: Legends Steakhouse
voyage.content: Part of the Creek Golf Clubhouse. The waterfront restaurant right on Dubai Creek is very popular with residents.

voyage.name: Al Bait Alqadeem Restaurant & Cafe
voyage.address: Al Ahmadiya St crossing 15a St, Al Ras
voyage.content: Emirati cuisine in an Emirati traditional house.

voyage.name: Floating Restaurants
voyage.hours: around 8PM daily for most of them
voyage.address: Baniyas Rd, Al Sabkha & Al Rigga & Rigga Al Buteen communities
voyage.content: Tens of dhows propose a diner during a 2-hour cruise on the creek.

voyage.name: JW's Steakhouse
voyage.content: This is the Marriott's signature restaurant. Very popular with Dubai residents.

voyage.name: Filli Cafeteria
voyage.content: Probably the most popular tea spots in town, especially Filli, who serves over 4,000 cups a day. Try the zaffrani chai (milk tea with saffron) or the doodh kadak (strong milk tea).

voyage.name: The Edge Pool & Bar
voyage.content: Small bar but wonderful views especially at sunset.

voyage.name: X Club
voyage.content: Russia-themed bar.

voyage.name: Dubai Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm from 100 dirhams or US$27, breakfast included
voyage.content: Reception 24/7. Pool, football field, chill-out garden, A/C in the room, small bar fridge. It's located next to a mosque so morning prayers may wake you. Stadium metro station and bus stop just 100 m from hostel, Lulu Hyper Market shopping center and supermarket nearby. Free safety deposit boxes (hang on to your key as they have stiff US$200 replacement fee). Clean rooms but unhelpful staff. You can walk there from T

voyage.name: Gulf Pearl Hotel
voyage.address: Al Baraha St, Omar al Khattab Rd
voyage.content: Rooms from 158 dirhams

voyage.name: Pacific Hotel
voyage.content: Rooms from 300 dirhams or US$80.

voyage.name: Niawara Guest House
voyage.content: Probably one of the cheapest places in town.

voyage.name: Alkhayam Hotel
voyage.address: Sikkat Al Khali Street, PO box 88249
voyage.content: free wifi, nice cafe

voyage.name: Qasr Al Seyaha Hotel
voyage.content: Another cheapy in the souk area

voyage.name: Al Jazeera Hotel
voyage.price: 220 dirhams dbl rm (200 dirhams if booked for 1 week)
voyage.address: PO box 8814, Al Ahmadea Rd, Al Ras Area

voyage.name: Galaxy Plaza
voyage.content: 2-star place, a step up from the under-200-dirham places.

voyage.name: Avari Dubai Hotel
voyage.content: Rooms from US$152.

voyage.name: Avenue Hotel
voyage.content: Rooms start at 350 dirhams, including breakfast.

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency Dubai
voyage.content: 414 rooms and suites with views of the Persian Gulf. Host to Al Dawaar, Dubai's only revolving restaurant.

voyage.name: InterContinental Residence Suites Dubai Festival City
voyage.content: Offers one-, two- and three-bedroom serviced suites with a choice between Creek and city views. Available for short or long stays.

voyage.name: Park Hyatt Dubai
voyage.content: Waterfront location next to the Dubai Creek Golf and Yacht Club.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel, Dubai Deira Creek
Taj Palace Hotel Dubai
voyage.content: Near Naif Square Bazaar.

voyage.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
voyage.address: Al Fahidi (19th) St crossing ManKhool Rd, north-east of Al Souk Al Kabeer community
voyage.content: One of the last remaining pockets of Old Dubai, home to many reconstructed buildings in the traditional style. While information on the structures is slim here (see the museum in preference), the atmosphere is very evocative and there are plenty of delightful art galleries and cafes to explore.

voyage.name: Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding
voyage.content: If you want to learn and understand the customs and traditions of UAE, this is the best place to go. The Centre hosts cultural meals for between 70 and 95 AED, with discussion of UAE culture, customs and religion. They run walking tours through the Bastakiya district for 60 minutes (35 AED) and 90 minutes (55 AED), starting at either 9 or 10:30AM daily except Friday.

voyage.name: Creek Park
voyage.content: A great place to hang out in the evening when the park is visited by people of different nationalities, all looking for calm place to enjoy the time. It has all the facilities of a modern park and is one of the best parks in Dubai. The cable car is closed.

voyage.name: Dubai Dolphinarium
voyage.content: The only indoor dolphinarium in the Middle East offers live shows of dolphins and seals. Swim with Dolphins is possible.

voyage.name: Dubai Museum
voyage.address: 11c Al Ibn Abi Talib St and 19 Al Fahidi St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community
voyage.content: A must-see for anyone interested in the social history of the Emirate (and indeed the country). Located in and under al-Fahidi fort. The fort itself has a few examples of the traditional reed houses and other artifacts, but isn't much to look at. The more interesting parts are the modern galleries beneath the fort, showcasing Dubai's history using the latest technology and culminating in a reconstructed souq from the

voyage.name: Grand Mosque
voyage.address: Ali bin Ali Taleb (11C) St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community
voyage.content: Its large minaret is the imposing feature of this large mosque. It is popular for being quite close to a Hindu temple and one can see followers of both Islam and Hinduism gathering at the same place for prayers.

voyage.name: Heritage Village
voyage.content: Home to the open museums of the Heritage and Diving Villages, and the houses of the late Sheikhs Saeed Al-Maktoum and Juma Al-Maktoum.

voyage.name: Iranian mosque
voyage.address: Ali bin Abi Taleb (11C) St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community
voyage.content: A very colourful and attractive tiled mosque; quite a contrast to the other much more plainly decorated mosques. Can be viewed from a carparking area off the north (creek) side of the street.

voyage.name: Sheikh Obaid bin Thani House
voyage.content: a historic building home to royal family members built in 1916 and now converted into a museum. It provides good glimpse to old infrastructure of Dubai.

voyage.name: Saeed Al Maktoum House
voyage.address: along the Dubai Creek in Al Shindagha
voyage.content: Another very historic building built in 1894 now converted into a museum and contains artefacts and images of the old town of Dubai. It was the residence of the Saeed bin Maktoum bin Hasher Al Maktoum, the former ruler of Dubai.

voyage.name: Crossroad of Civilization Museum
voyage.address: Sheikh Hasher bin Maktoum Al Maktoum Home, Al Mina Rd, Shindagha Heritage area, POBox 46298
voyage.content: Museum includes a lot of artefacts and old books, including a Gutenberg Bible and a curtain of the door of Kaaba from 1543 AD.

voyage.name: Old Weapons Museum
voyage.content: Large collection of swords, daggers, riffles, from several centuries.

voyage.name: Manuscript, Old Book and Print Museum
Zabeel Park
voyage.address: Sheik Khalifa Bin Zayed St and Sheik Rashid Rd, Al Kefaf community
voyage.content: The best and most popular park of town, it gives a remarkable glimpse of the desert and hot Dubai.

voyage.name: Dubai Frame
voyage.content: Two towers of 150 m height connected by a 100-m² bridge, the Dubai Frame has a museum and gallery where you can see the growth of Dubai from a simple fishing village to the ultra-modern city it is today with the use of photos and advanced technology. After visiting the museum, you take the elevator to the bridge to get a view of the city.

voyage.name: Dubai Ferry trip
voyage.price: 50 dirhams/person in regular, 75 dirhams/person in gold class
voyage.address: Al Ghubaiba Marine Transport Station, Al Ghubaiba Rd, Al Shindagha community
voyage.content: The Dubai Ferry makes a sightseeing circular trip to Jumeirah Beach (deep sea side) or to the Floating Bridge (toward the creek). There are also a one way trips towards Dubai Marina at 1pm and 6pm (duration: 2 hours).

voyage.name: Dubai Textile Souk
voyage.address: between the creek and Ali Bin Abi Taleb (11C) St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community
voyage.content: A lot of shops selling scarves and keffiyeh. A few of the shopkeepers can be quite forceful in trying to get you in to their shop.

voyage.name: BurJuman
voyage.address: Sheikh Ralifa Rd, Al Mankhool community
voyage.content: A 4-floor shopping mall housing more than 300 stores. It is one of the oldest, and still one of the largest, malls in Dubai, but has become less popular.

voyage.name: Computer Plaza @ Al-Ain Centre
voyage.content: A mall specializing in computers, laptops, computer parts and computer add-ons like monitors, VoIP phones, hard drives, etc. Prices aren't particularly low, even after haggling, and choices are limited (for example very few shops sell AMD hardware). There used to be an internet cafe here and it may return in 2014. Other malls in this area are also good for computers and computer equipment.

voyage.name: Lamcy Plaza
voyage.address: Sheikh Rashid Rd, Oud Metha community
voyage.content: A 3 story shopping mall housing more than 150 stores. One of the oldest malls.

voyage.name: Wafi Mall & Khan Murjan Souk
voyage.address: Sheikh Rashid Rd, Oud Metha Rd, Umm Hurair 2 community, POBox 721
voyage.content: Includes Marks & Spencer, Goodies. Focus is almost entirely on luxury brands, jewellery and expensive boutiques. Many upmarket restaurants and bars, many of which serve alcohol. A luxury spa is attached to the complex. The Egypt-themed architecture, which includes quite beautiful stained-glass pyramids, is worth seeing.

voyage.name: Gharana
voyage.content: Gharana an Indian Restaurant in Holiday Inn Dubai – Al Barsha hotel brings you flavors of various spices and herbs with live entertainment.

voyage.name: Basta Art Cafe
voyage.content: Set in a lovely garden courtyard in a restored house. Great place to take a breather with a cold drink and write some postcards. The sandwiches-and-salads menu is aimed squarely at tourists, but if you are sick of kebabs, they will cater to your salmon-avocado wrap and mango smoothie cravings. The "Basta Special" drink of mint and lemon is also excellent.

voyage.name: Gazebo
voyage.content: Very nice and warm welcome given by the waiters. Food as good too. Not so expensive when compared to the quality of food.

voyage.name: Ravi Restaurant
voyage.content: A Pakistani restaurant that provides cheap Pakistani & Indian food. Good for anyone with a spicy tooth.

voyage.name: Student Biryani
voyage.content: A Pakistani restaurant serving the country's most popular biryani.

voyage.name: Local House
voyage.address: House 51, Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, 19 Al Fahidi St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community
voyage.content: Emirati cuisine featuring camel meats and camel milkshakes in a traditional Dubai house.

voyage.name: Al Haj Bundu Khan
voyage.content: Indian and Pakistani food.

voyage.name: Pars Iranian Kitchen
voyage.content: This is an open air Iranian restaurant where one can sit in traditional machans (large bed-like seating) and enjoy a fine Iranian meal. The speciality is the mixed grill which is served with live coal. After the meal, you may smoke a traditional sheesha pipe. No alcohol served.

voyage.name: Wafi Gourmet
voyage.content: Excellent Lebanese cuisine and ambience. In the cooler months the outdoor verandah is a pleasure. No alcohol served.

voyage.name: Yakitori House
voyage.address: Century Hotel, Khalid Bin Walid St, Bur Dubai
voyage.content: Japanese cuisine, very popular with the Japanese expat community.

voyage.name: Asha's
voyage.content: Indian cuisine. Run by Asha Bosle. Good food but a little expensive

voyage.name: Manhattan Grill
voyage.content: Fine dining restaurant with New York-inspired cuisine, specialising in steak. A suitable venue for romantic dinners and family gatherings.

voyage.name: Barrels Pub
voyage.content: It is a bar is a clean, quiet and bright venue with large variates of snacks options. Every wall is mounted with screen playing number of sports games. The interiors looks good with polished timber tables and benches all around and wall cladding.

voyage.name: Bollywood Café
voyage.content: Excellent DJ, Live music and Indian food. It is a Bollywood-themed glamorous bar and nightlife with elegant to casual laid backs and pleasant musical twists, mostly Indian music.

voyage.name: Chill Rooftop Lounge
voyage.content: Dance floor with excellent DJ. It is an expansive rooftop venue painted in pink surrounded with fake grass. An outdoor seating place with good food.

voyage.name: Marine's Club
voyage.content: A lively bar and nightclub with 80s music most of the time. It is a budget friendly venue with great service and superb bouncers.

voyage.name: Ascot Hotel
voyage.content: Has Russian, Irish and Thai themed restaurants. Rooms from AED $180.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Dubai
voyage.content: A resort style hotel with extensive conference facilities and 13 restaurants serving cuisine from all over the world.

voyage.name: Raffles Dubai
voyage.content: Attached to Wafi Mall. Egyptian themed.

voyage.name: Burj al-Arab
voyage.price: Overnight stays over US$1800 per night after taxes/fees
voyage.content: This huge sail-shaped hotel completed in 1999 is a symbol of Dubai and its ascent in the world. The self-proclaimed world's first seven-star hotel (actually a five-star deluxe hotel) was the first icon of Dubai and still stands out on the skyline from its location on an artificial island 280 m from the beach. Entry to the hotel is restricted to hotel guests, those with a restaurant reservation (minimum spend 200AED)

voyage.name: Burj Khalifa
voyage.price: Tickets cost 199 dirham for a timed-entry ticket, usually later the same day, or 400 dirham if you do not want to wait. The lines for tickets are often very long and at peak times, they can sell out several days in advance. It is strongly recommended to book tickets online ahead of your visit. For 500 dirham you can book a "SKY" ticket that includes a trip to level 148 of the building (which is relatively empty and exclusive) for 30 minutes, along with sweets and drinks. From there, you descend to the main observatory on levels 125 and 124 to join the masses waiting to go back down. The SKY ticket also includes a brief tour of the building's private areas. If you go for 'sunrise+breakfast' option for 140 dirham you can visit floor 124 at 05:30 and after, with floor 125 opening at 08:30 - this is a great way to avoid the queues and see the city during both night and day
voyage.content: At 828 m and 160 floors this is the world's tallest structure by a long shot, over 300 m taller than the previous contender in Taipei. The observation deck at the 124th floor is the second highest in the world after the Shanghai World Financial centre. Dominating the Dubai skyline, the tower houses a hotel and a Las Vegas-inspired fountain system. The visitors' entrance is at the lower ground floor of Dubai Mall. Alt

voyage.name: Dubai Fountain
voyage.hours: Day shows are at 13:00 and 13:30, but night shows are the best - every 30 minutes 18:00-22:00 on weekdays and 18:00-23:00 on weekends.
voyage.content: At 270m (900 ft) in length and sporting a jet that shoots water up to 150m (500 ft), it is the world's largest dancing fountain and one with a very enticing display - a definite must-see. It's most easily accessed via the Dubai Mall. There are private entranceways from the Burj Khalifa if you're staying there.

voyage.name: Dubai Marina
voyage.content: The Dubai Marina is to be the popular nightlife area of Dubai in the future. This multi-billion-dollar development is designed for tourists and water sport. The bars and cafés along the marina are popular gathering points for families and younger people. Most restaurants offer shisha and oriental food but food chains are fast entering too. The "Marina Walk" along the yachts is especially popular on Fridays and Saturd

voyage.name: Jumeirah Beach
voyage.content: Dubai is known for its great beaches and this one is the best. It's the most popular and busiest beach of the country. Expect to see swimmers in bikinis and ladies in abaya cloaks; this beach truly encapsulates the Westernisation of Dubai culture.

voyage.name: Jumeirah Mosque
voyage.content: The largest mosque in the city, and a wonderful example of Islamic architecture. It was built in the medieval Fatimid tradition with the interior decorated with elaborate Arabic calligraphy. It is one of few mosques in the city open for visits by non-Muslims; the Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding conducts special tours for non-Muslims to help promote understanding of Islam. Guided tours are available

voyage.name: Majlis Ghorfat Umm Al Sheif
voyage.price: 1 dirham for adults and children over 6 years
voyage.content: A restored traditional Emirati-style two story building used as a summer residence by Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum, one of the founders of UAE, and father of the present ruler of Dubai.

voyage.name: Palm Islands
voyage.content: The Palm islands are the best symbols of the boom and bust construction cycles in Dubai. The "oldest" Palm called Palm Jumeirah is completed and is host to the gigantic Atlantis Hotel on its top. Several marinas, hotels and condo are along the palm leaves. Palm Jumeirah has the densest collection of beach clubs in the city, which are popular with locals and tourists alike. Some beach clubs are part of hotels, while o

voyage.name: Al Safa Park
voyage.address: Al Hadiqa Rd, Al Safa community
voyage.content: A beautiful planned park and one of the oldest parks in Dubai. It is a favourite for sports enthusiasts, and many visitors enjoy playing tennis, volleyball, and soccer. Children love playing games in the video arcade, or riding the Ferris wheel and bumper cars. The park even has a maze to wander through. Barbeques and picnic areas are available for those who want to make a day of it. It has lakes where you can take a

voyage.name: Etihad Museum
voyage.address: 2nd December Rd crossing Jumeirah Rd, Jumeirah 1 community
voyage.content: Museum about the construction of the Union of the Emirates, after the withdrawal of British forces. Open in 2017, it features exhibits about the seven fathers, and the constitution. The Union House, where the treaty was signed, can be visited as well as the Guest Palace. It also hosts temporary exhibitions (e.g., philatelic in May 2017).

voyage.name: Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo
voyage.price: Researcher Experience for 100 dirham/person, Explorer Experience for 120 dirham/person, VIP for 300 dirham/person
voyage.address: Dubai Mall, Doha St, Sheikh Zayed Rd
voyage.content: Giant aquarium, 51 m long and 11 m high. The visit includes a crossing inside the walk-through water tunnel, behind the scenes, and several other experiences. The Underwater Zoo has 140 fish species, desert animals, penguins and also hosts "King Krok". Animal feeding hours are indicated in the zoo, and it's also possible to participate during feeding.

voyage.name: Museum of the Future
voyage.address: Emirates Towers, Sheikh Zayed Rd, Trade Center 2 community
voyage.content: Branded as a "technology museum" many visitors consider it more of an expensive art exhibition. The building is outstanding though and looks particularly impressive in the dark.

voyage.name: Jumeirah Fishing Harbor
voyage.address: Jumeirah Rd crossing 311 Al Urouba Rd, Jumeirah 1 community
voyage.content: A quiet place with some nice restaurants.

voyage.name: The Lost Chambers Aquarium and Ambassador Lagoon
voyage.price: 110 dirhams/adult, 80 dirham/child below 11, discounts for UAE residents, 30 dirham for Ambassador Lagoon only
voyage.address: Atlantis, Cresent Rd East, Palm Jumeirah
voyage.content: An Atlantis-themed aquarium with a lot of fish species and jellyfishes. Don't miss the giant chamber with numerous sharks and rays. Shark feeding 10:15 and 15:45, ray feeding at 09:30 and 15:15. Possibilities to dive or do the "Aqua Trek" in the Ambassador Lagoon.

voyage.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
voyage.content: A coloful and well maintained garden with more than 45 million flowers and numerous sculptures made out of flowers. Some visitors found it a bit too kitschy.

voyage.name: Emirates Towers
voyage.content: The Emirates Towers complex contains the Emirates Office Tower and Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel. The two towers, which rise to 355 m (1,165 ft) and 309 m (1,014 ft), respectively, stand as the 23rd and 47th tallest buildings in the world. The two towers are connected by a 9,000 m² (96,875 ft²) two-storey retail complex known as "The Boulevard". The Emirates Towers complex is located on the Sheikh Zayed Road in Duba

voyage.name: The View at The Palm
voyage.content: Observation deck, 5-star hotel, luxury apartments. See the spectacular views over Palm Jumeirah.

voyage.name: Sky Views Dubai
voyage.address: Sky Views, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Blvd
voyage.content: This hotel building offers beautiful views toward Burj Khalifa from its 53rd floor observation deck. There is a 25-m glass floor walk and a ride on a glass slide included. For another dirham a walk along the edge of this building floor can be booked.

voyage.name: Cycling or walking along Jumeirah Beach
voyage.content: A beautiful coastal running and cycling track stretches for about 7 km from the mouth of Dubai Canal all the way to Burj Al Arab. One of the few places in Dubai where you can see native Emiratis enjoying their time alongside expats from all over the world in the evenings. There are bike rental stations along the way (mobile data and a credit card needed though).

voyage.name: Ski Dubai
voyage.price: A "Slope Session" pass costs 200 dirhams for 2 hours or 300 dirhams for full day, plus 20 dirhams, for a locker. The "Snow Park" starts at 190 dirhams, the pack with all activities unlimited "Ski Dubai Experience" costs 500 dirhams
voyage.hours: Sun–Wed 10:00–23:00, Thu 10:00–00:00, Fri 09:00–00:00, Sat 09:00-23:00 – tickets close 1 hr 30 min before
voyage.address: Mall of Emirates, Sheikh Zayed Rd crossing Umm Suqueim Rd, Al Barsha 1
voyage.content: Dubai has a snow skiing centre in the Mall of the Emirates, offering both skiing and snowboarding. The 400 m slope is quite large for an indoor area. All equipment is available for hire. Although it is inside, you do not need to bring a jacket because they supply pretty much everything except gloves and a hat which you can buy right there (gloves are included in some packs). It also propose the "Penguin Encounter" ac

voyage.name: Wild Wadi Waterpark
voyage.hours: 10:00–19:00 daily, sometimes closes at 18:00 for private events
voyage.content: The perfect place for the entire family to spend a day as well as being a great way to beat the heat and enjoy the day away from the bustle of the city. Located close to the hotels and resorts of Jumeriah Beach, the park has water rides, slides, and a lagoon that is hidden away. You'll enjoy waterfalls, out of the way swimming holes, and a tidal pool.

voyage.name: Atlantis
voyage.content: Atlantis-themed but Arabian-styled resort on the artificial island of The Palm. Has a huge water park with plenty of thrilling water slides, an aquarium and a large shopping area with plenty of places to eat and drink.

voyage.name: Aquaventure Waterpark
voyage.price: 320 dirham/adults 275 dirham/child under 1.2 m, 40 dirhams for locker, discounts via online booking
voyage.address: Atlantis, Cresent Rd East, Palm Jumeirah
voyage.content: Aquaventure have a lot of water slides, including the extreme slides: Leap of feath and Poseidon's Revenge. It also includes Dolphin encounter, swimming with dolphins. The waterpark also contains the Dubai Balloon, which offers 10min balloon rides up to 300m high for AED 175 (adults) and AED 75 (children).

voyage.name: Skydive Dubai
voyage.content: Tandem jumps over the Palm Jumeirah or the desert. Gyrocopter flights available as well.

voyage.name: Megaplex
voyage.content: Experience the next generation of cinemas and impressive effects in the Middle East. You can also book tickets via app or online.

voyage.name: Dubai Marina Yacht Club
voyage.content: A quiet and peaceful place with colorful lights at the night. You can rent a boat for a few hours or a day or just sit there for hours watching the skyscrapers and eating out at great restaurants.

voyage.name: XLine
voyage.content: The world's longest urban zip line.

voyage.name: Ibn Battuta Mall
voyage.content: The pavilions are themed according to the voyages of the great voyager Ibn Battuta. Areas themed around six countries (China, India, Persia, Egypt, Tunisia and the Andalusia). Wide range of shops, although fewer high class brands. Has various restaurants and cafes (including three Starbucks), and a multiplex cinema including an Imax. No restaurants serve alcohol. Also has extensive, permanent exhibition of Islamic sc

voyage.name: The Dubai Mall
voyage.content: The largest mall in the world, it opened in 2008. It has over 1,200 shops of brand names from all over the world. It contains an indoor ice rink and indoor aquarium. It is right next door to the Burj Khalifah, and the visitors' entrance to the Burj Khalifa is located at the lower ground floor of the Mall. It houses the Dubai Aquarium (which you can dive tours in) and 1,200 shops for everything. The food court on the

voyage.name: Boulevard – Jumeirah Emirates Towers
voyage.address: Emirates Towers, Sheikh Zayed Rd, Trade Center 2 community
voyage.content: Part of the Emirates Tower Hotel complex. The shops here match the hotel, very high class, plus a Starbucks. Lipton café has free Wi-Fi. Restaurants and bars all serve alcohol. Quite a popular nightlife spot, with bars and nightclubs and it is considered the most expensive mall in Dubai.

voyage.name: Mall of the Emirates
voyage.hours: Outside Ramadan: Sun–Wed 10:00–22:00, Thu–Sat 10:00–00:00; Ramadan: daily 10:00-01:00
voyage.address: Near 4th interchange on Sheikh Zayed Rd, Al Barsha 1 community
voyage.content: It was largest shopping mall outside of North America until the Dubai Mall opened in 2008. Over 200 shops, cinemas, plus the Ski Centre. Has many international high street chains as well as luxury brand stores, including Harvey Nichols. Many restaurants and cafés, though cafés tend to be much more crowded than at other malls. It's attached to a Kempinski hotel, which has restaurants licensed to serve alcohol that are

voyage.name: Mercato
voyage.content: Mercato (Italian for market) is the only Renaissance-themed shopping mall in the Middle East. It captures Italian, French and Spanish flavors and artistic characteristics, playing host to regular fairs and festivals from each country. Mercato provides a unique shopping experience, the best in international entertainment and popular brand names like Virgin Megastore, Top Shop, Mango and Hugo Boss; Mercato is simply Th

voyage.name: Souk Madinat Jumeirah
voyage.content: Includes 75 shops, numerous bars, restaurants and cafés, a nightclub, theatre. More expensive and targeted directly at tourists than other, general malls where residents go. Most bars and restaurants are licensed for alcohol. Nice to wander through as it has been designed to resemble a "traditional" souq, but with the modern comforts of air conditioning. Lots of souvenir-type shops.Dubai - Souk Madinat Jumeirah - pan

voyage.name: Town Centre Jumeirah
voyage.content: With a bright, open and spacious atmosphere, it is a place to shop, relax and casually dine at a wide selection of eateries like Sumo Sushi, Cafe Ceramique, La Cafette by Carpe Diem and Simply Healthy. It also houses an extensive range of ladies' beauty outlets like the Nail Station, Paris Gallery, Kaya Skin Care Clinic, Wax Lounge and SOS Salon.

voyage.name: Satwa
voyage.content: A small community much resembling a town, its streets are rowed by textile shops notably opposite the Satwa Mosque ending to the opposite of Satwa clinic. Most of the people flock to Satwa for their textiles, you might sometimes catch offers and discounts but if you don't do so try bargaining the price, this is what most locals do, even if you're a tourist convince the salesman to give you a discount, bargain till yo

voyage.name: Dubai Marina Mall
voyage.content: Another mall, with cinema, food court, etc.

voyage.name: Oasis Center
voyage.content: Contains retail space of about 1 million sq. ft. and total area of 1.44 million sq. ft. It has wide varieties brands and diverse categories related to beauty, lifestyle, luxury, home decor, furnishing, shoe, sports, electronics, etc. Not just a mall but it also housed spas, saloons, markets, fitness center, cafes, etc. Its two basement parking facility (approx 470,000 sq. ft.) can accommodate approx 1,700 vehicles.

voyage.name: Times Square Center
voyage.address: Sheikh Zayed Road, At 3/4th Interchange, Dubai
voyage.content: A unique mall with exclusive shopping experiences across Dubai. It is different than the rest of the malls in Dubai.

voyage.name: Emirates Official Store
voyage.address: Mezzanine Floor, dnata Travel Centre, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: You can shop Emirates merchandise from the Emirates Official Store that offers offers travel accessories, toys, caps, bags, executive items, collectible lapel pins, numerous aircraft models and other aviation collectables.

voyage.name: 800 Pizza
voyage.content: Traditional & authentic Italian pizza baked in wood fired Italian stone oven, thin & crispy crust.

voyage.name: More Cafe
voyage.content: Serves breakfast, lunch and light continental and oriental meals. Good service and big portions.

voyage.name: Noodle House
voyage.address: Emirates Towers Shopping Blvd, Madinat Jumeirah
voyage.content: Asian food.

voyage.name: Chill Out
voyage.address: Times Square Centre, Ground F, Sheihk Zayed Rd, Al Marabea St, Al Quoz community
voyage.content: Have a delicious contemporary European food in ice lounge at a chilling temperature of . It is first of its kind in the Middle East. From tables to even crockery in which food is served, all made of ice.

voyage.name: Chimes
voyage.content: Thai, Singaporean, Malaysian and Indonesian themed food, and the popular house speciality must be the pepper or chili crab. You can eat at the restaurant or order home delivery to most areas of new Dubai.

voyage.name: Jedoudna Restaurant
voyage.address: Rimal Sector, The Walk at Jumeirah Beach Residence
voyage.content: A family-run Lebanese restaurant. With outdoor seating and separate shisha area.

voyage.name: Karam Beirut
voyage.address: 1st floor, Mall of Emirates, Sheykh Zayed Rd, Al Barsha
voyage.content: Excellent Lebanese food.

voyage.name: Lal Qila Dubai
voyage.content: Pakistani cuisine.

voyage.name: London Fish & Chips
voyage.address: Tunisia Food Court, Ibn Batutta Mall, Jebel Ali Village
voyage.content: Fish, chips, sharky meals, traditional battered, baked potatoes, sandwiches, salads and soups

voyage.name: Toscana
voyage.content: Italian.

voyage.name: Al Fresco
voyage.address: Crowne Plaza, Dubai, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: Specialized in Italian food with cosy outdoor seating. Business lunch, Family friendly place. Smoking and alcohol is permitted. Try the garlic bruschetta with traditional tomato, the leafy green salad, oozy burrata cheese, tomato, sprinkled with drizzles of balsamic vinegar.

voyage.name: Al Mahara
voyage.content: Part of the Burj Al Arab hotel, and as you would expect is also very high quality, especially seafood.

voyage.name: At.mosphere
voyage.content: Exclusive fine dining restaurant on Level 122 of Burj Khalifa.

voyage.name: The Gem Garden
voyage.address: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: Continental restaurant.

voyage.name: Gharana
voyage.address: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: Authentic Indian restaurant.

voyage.name: Margaux
voyage.address: Souk al Bahar, opp dubai mall fountains
voyage.content: European, steak and continental cuisine. Pleasing and stunning ambiance with variations and one could enjoy the views of Burj Khalifa and the fountain shows.

voyage.name: Options, by Sanjeev Kapoor
voyage.content: Run by famed Indian TV chef Sanjeev Kapoor. Drinks served. Reservations recommended especially on Friday nights.

voyage.name: The Royal Budha
voyage.address: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: Authentic Thai restaurant.

voyage.name: Shang Palace
voyage.address: Level 1, Shangri-La Hotel, Shk Zayed Rd
voyage.content: Good Chinese food. No smoking

voyage.name: Al Nafoorah
voyage.address: Jumeirah, Emirates Towers Boulevard, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: Arabic, Lebanese and Middle Eastern cuisines. Outdoor seating with perfect sense of fine dining accompanied with comfortable, Arabian-style terrace. Smoking and alcohol is permitted.

Jumeirah Beach Hotel Complex. Open air bar with great views of the Burj hotel and the Jumeirah beach hotel all helped by a cool breeze from the ocean. Various DJs but think Ibiza lounge bar and you will not be far off.

voyage.name: Buddha Bar
voyage.address: Grosvenor House Dubai, Al Sufouh Rd
voyage.content: Branch of the international Asian-themed bar/restaurant. Full of crowds.

voyage.name: Barasti
voyage.content: Built in three levels (each playing its own music), with lounging areas on the beach, lots of young and foreign people come here during the weekend. Very popular with expats.

voyage.name: Nasimi Beach
voyage.content: Great bar/club on the beach in the Palm Jumeirah.

voyage.name: Long's Bar
voyage.content: The longest bar in the UAE, typical English style with live football, similar to a UK Wetherspoons. Great music and DJs plus food and friendly atmosphere.

voyage.name: Left Bank
voyage.content: O the waterfront in one of the most tranquil areas of Dubai. A great food menu leads on to some excellent cocktails and music inside.

voyage.name: Observatory
voyage.content: Bar and restaurant with great view across Palm Jumeirah (on a clear day!) Popular happy hour with the after work crowd on Thursday from 18:00-20:00.

voyage.name: Skyview Bar
voyage.content: Live local and international bands, reservations are a must.

voyage.name: Vu's Bar
voyage.content: Try the 51st Floor house cocktail, it's so deliciously strong, also there's a staggering 200 cocktails to choose from.

voyage.name: Zero Gravity
voyage.content: Beach club, a nice place for partying.

voyage.name: VIP Room
voyage.address: JW Marriott, Marquis Hotel Dubai, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: It is a lounge-like lively space that offers mid-range to high-price drinks. The huge multi-color circular space is cornered by large LCD screens and exclusive tables and the scantily clad podium dancers.

voyage.name: The Act
voyage.content: This venue is full of dance artists, mischievous performances, women performing unusual stunts and on-stage antics. It is a place where you will forget that you are in Dubai. The drinks are good and are slightly over priced but this place will make you feels liberated, little bit different and edgy.

voyage.name: The Cigar Bar
voyage.content: Specialized in true cigar aficionado, cognacs and whiskies. Smoking is permitted. Dresscode is smart casuals. It is a traditional venue with modern rich dark enveloping and mahogany lined interior furnishing. The Cigar Bar will be closed during the Holy Month of Ramadan

voyage.name: Zinc
voyage.address: Crowne Plaza Dubai, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: It is the city’s most popular nightclubs with girls night out, dance floor and variety of DJ sets. This place is always over crowded and the drinks are budget friendly.

voyage.name: The Address Downtown Dubai
voyage.address: Mohammed Bin Rashid Boulevard, Downtown Dubai
voyage.content: One of the many luxury hotels next to Burj Khalifa with many good fine dining restaurants and bars.

voyage.name: Anantara The Palm Dubai Resort
voyage.content: Houses the only over water villas in the UAE.

voyage.name: Atlantis, the Palm
voyage.content: Hotel on the Palm. Connects to mainland by monorail.

voyage.name: Fairmont Dubai
voyage.content: Closest 5-star hotel to the World Trade Centre.

voyage.name: Fraser Suites Dubai
voyage.address: Sidra Tower, Sheikh Zayed Road, Media City
voyage.content: Serviced apartments and accommodation.

voyage.name: Hilton Dubai Jumeirah
voyage.address: Tower A, The Walk, Jumeirah Beach Residence
voyage.content: Resort with a private beach. The hotel is only 10 floors which is dwarfed by nearby high-rises, but the location is lively and the pool/garden area is lush.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha
voyage.content: 310 elegant rooms, a choice of 3 bars, choice of 2 fine dining restaurants and 6-storey high atrium and piano lounge. Gymnasium, roof top pool, massage rooms, sauna and spa.

voyage.name: Jumeirah Beach Hotel
voyage.content: Next to Burj al-Arab and run by the same company.

voyage.name: The Radisson Blu Residence, Dubai Marina
voyage.address: Plot No. 392-260 Street K Dubai Marina
voyage.content: 5 km away from Jafza, and economic free zone. It has 152 apartments with scenic balcony, two restaurants with the convenience of onsite dining. They arrange variety of events from time to time.

voyage.name: Chelsea Gardens Hotel Apartments
voyage.content: It has 169 well-appointed luxury comfortable and spacious apartment suites with modern interior. Upon request, they offer airport transfers.

voyage.name: Emirates Grand Hotel
voyage.address: Near Finance Centre, Metro Stop, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: It is a non-alcoholic hotel decorated with luxurious amenities. Equipped with stream rooms, hot tubs, sauna, roof top pool, fitness center and tennis court.

voyage.name: Dusit Thani Dubai
voyage.content: Beautiful surroundings with Asian hospitality and teak-wood furniture all around and Venetian blinds. champagne lounge available. They have 321 modern rooms equipped with high-speed Internet connections.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha
voyage.address: Near Mall of The Emirates, E11 Sheikh Zayed Rd
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hilton Dubai Al Habtoor City
voyage.address: Al Habtoor City, Sheikh Zayed Road
voyage.content: The hotel is 44 floors and has 1004 guest rooms, 8 dining outlets and 21 meeting rooms. 10 minutes by car from Downtown Dubai.

voyage.name: Th8 Palm Dubai Beach Resort
voyage.content: Beachfront resort.

voyage.name: Anantara World Islands Dubai Resort
voyage.content: Beachfront resort located on the World Islands. Contains a Swimming pool, spa, Paddle court, Fitness centre, Water sports centre, Kids’ club and Games room

voyage.name: The Heart of Europe
voyage.content: Complex of several European-themed hotels spanning six islands in the Europe section of the World Islands. Includes Spanish-themed Marbella resort, four French Riviera-themed hotels (complete with marketplace and discotheque), Italian-themed Portofino Hotel, British-inspired Hotel London, Artist Hotel, the Danish-style Hygge Hotel, the Sweden Beach house, and 133 floating villas

voyage.name: Port of Jebel Ali
voyage.content: The world's largest man-made harbour and the biggest port in the Middle East. It was constructed in the late 1970s to supplement the facilities at Port Rashid. It is located thirty-five kilometres southwest of Dubai, in the Persian Gulf. On April 9, 2011 Jebel Ali Port won the Golden Award for Best Seaport Overall from the Higher Committee for UAE Civil Seaports and Airports Security.

voyage.name: Jebel Ali Shooting Club
voyage.content: This club has awesome architecture and design. It has wide range of shooting options to practice right from automatic ball trap, Olympic trap, down the line, Olympic skeet to compak sporting.

voyage.name: Switch Bowling
voyage.content: A multi-lane bowling section, one of the perfect indoor entertainment venue for families and kids. In addition, it has billiards section, video gaming areas, toddlers' play area and restaurants.

voyage.name: Peekaboo!
voyage.content: An ideal place for children below 7 years, for entertaining and creative activities. There is a variety of play equipment, toys and classes for kids.

voyage.name: Seawings
voyage.content: Experience live areal views and sightseeing excursions of Dubai's modern skyline and dazzling landmarks. The water-based take-offs and landings further adds greater experience.

voyage.name: Jetty Lounge
voyage.content: This is an elegant beach lounge that has fantastic drinks. Cozy, but over-crowded during the sunsets.

voyage.name: Oasis Town of Dahid
voyage.content: Explore the village, its traditions and the oasis.

voyage.name: Dubai Parks & Resorts
voyage.content: Dubai Parks and Resorts is the Middle East's largest integrated leisure and theme park destination featuring more than 100 rides and attractions, and consists of three theme parks: Motiongate Dubai, Bollywood Parks Dubai, and Legoland Dubai, and one water park: Legoland Water Park. It also encompasses Riverland Dubai, which is a themed retail and dining destination, as well as the Polynesian-themed family resort, Lap

voyage.name: Jebel Ali Club
voyage.address: Old Jabel Ali Village, Near Ibn Battuta Mall (Sheikh Zayed Rd), Dubai
voyage.content: A good restaurant with relaxing pub, pools, darts, swimming pool and steam rooms. The drink and food is budget friendly.

voyage.name: The Kebab Shop
voyage.content: Good budget friendly food specialized in British, Pakistani, Indian and Turkish food

voyage.name: Kcal Healthy Fast Food
voyage.content: Healthy fast food and great dining experience.

voyage.name: Chicken Tikka Inn
voyage.content: Awesome place for great Indian food.

voyage.name: La Fontana
voyage.address: JA Palm Tree Court, Ground Floor, next to the La Fontana Swimming Pool
voyage.content: Mediterranean cuisine, generous breakfast buffet, international dishes and a variety of themed dinner buffets, either indoors or on the large outdoor terrace.

voyage.name: Mushref Bar
voyage.address: JA Jebel Ali, Beach Hotel, Jebel Ali
voyage.content: Shaded by palm trees with numerous pool bars, entertainment zones and sunbeds.

voyage.name: Palmito Pool Bar
voyage.address: JA Palm Tree Court, Jebel Ali, Dubai
voyage.content: Swim-up pool bar serving good drinks and refreshments.

voyage.name: Sunset Lounge
voyage.address: JA Jebel Ali Beach Hotel, Jebel Ali
voyage.content: Great Beverages.

voyage.name: Diablo Nightclub Dubai
voyage.address: Ibn Battuta Gate Hotel in Jebel Ali
voyage.content: It is a Moroccan Themed lounge that serves cocktails, shisha, teas and coffees.

voyage.name: The Bar
voyage.address: Courtyard by Marriott Dubai Green Community
voyage.content: Casual lounge with indoor and al fresco seating. It serves beverages, cocktails, light snacks and light dishes.

voyage.name: Jebel Ali Beach Hotel
voyage.address: Exit 13, Sheikh Zayed Road, Jebel Ali, Dubai
voyage.content: Pets are not allowed. Speaks Russian, English, German and Arabic. This luxurious resort hotel is located on the Arabian Gulf. It has 1km private beach surrounded by palm trees and sun loungers. All the rooms are bright and stylish and they have fresh air and scenic balcony.

voyage.name: Premier Inn Dubai Investments Park Hotel
voyage.content: This hotel offers, business services, multilingual staff, free wi-fi, Video Conferencing, night clubs, casinos, safe deposit box and swimming pool.

voyage.name: Mushrif Park
voyage.price: entrance fee 10 dirhams per car; to use the swimming pool, adults pay 10 dirhams and children pay 5 dirhams
voyage.content: Mushrif Park is 5.25-km² (1300-acre) desert-like park. It is in the eastern part of the city (near the suburb of Khawaneej), about 16 km (10 mi) from the traditional center of Dubai. The park was created in early 1980 by Dubai Municipality and was hugely expanded and refurbished in 1989.

voyage.name: Imagine
voyage.hours: Sat-Wed 8PM 9PM 10PM, Thu Fri 8PM 9PM 10PM 11PM, smaller shows play every 30&nbps;min from 6PM
voyage.address: Festival Bay, Dubai Festival City, Festival Blvd
voyage.content: Plays two different big water, fire and light shows: Stardancer and A Child's Dream. Have several world records.

voyage.name: Global Village
voyage.address: Exit #37 on Sh Mohammed Bin Zayed Rd
voyage.content: Annual festival (usually during winter). Countries around the world gather and set up a small village in the outskirts of Dubai. Each country/region has its own pavilion with a unique replica of their famous landmarks. This is usually like a flea market where you can get souvenirs from almost every corner of the earth for a bargained price and experience as if you're in that certain country for at least 10 minutes of

voyage.name: Dubai Autodrome
voyage.content: This is 5-km world-class motorsports circuit hosted many international championships. You can take thrilling driving experience here in some of the world's fastest sports cars.

voyage.name: IMG Worlds of Adventure
voyage.address: City of Arabia, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Rd E311
voyage.content: A very large indoor theme park, with 4 universes: Lost Valley, IMG boulverard, Cartoon Network, Marvell. Nice families and adventurers, specially during hot summer months. It has 22 attractions including 3 roller coasters: The Velociraptor (5 inversions), Predator (3 inversions) and Spiderman (turning seats).

voyage.name: Dubai Sports City (DSC)
voyage.content: A 50-million square feet mixed use development that will be the world’s first integrated purpose-built sports city. The development is being built around five major sports venues and features a series of major sports academy facilities. It contains these sporting complexes:

voyage.name: DSC Multi-Purpose Stadium
voyage.content: The main sports structure will be a 60,000-seat multi-purpose outdoor stadium. This stadium will be used for athletics, cricket and football.

voyage.name: Dubai International Stadium
voyage.content: A 25,000-seat cricket stadium, popularly known as Ring of Fire.

voyage.name: DSC Indoor Arena
voyage.content: A 10,000-seat indoor arena.

voyage.name: Rugby Park
voyage.content: A 5,000-seat field hockey stadium. The stadium will provide a base to the UAE Hockey Committee and the WorldHockey Academy. The Hockey Stadium is situated at the Dubai Sports City Academy's Campus and provides world-class facilities for international athletes and local enthusiasts. The World Hockey Academy is the first facility of its kind anywhere in the world. Through a partnership between Dubai Sports City and the

voyage.name: Dubai Safari Park
voyage.content: Dubai Safari Park is a wildlife park, animal sanctuary & education center that is home to more than 2,500 animals from all over the world including lions, elephants, giraffes, moon bears, and camels. The park is divided into four zones - Explorer Village, African Village, Arabian Desert Safari, and Asian Village.

voyage.name: Dubai Outlet Mall
voyage.address: Route E 66 (the road to Al Ain)
voyage.content: A very large mall, with many "factory outlets".

voyage.name: Mall of Arabia
voyage.content: Mall of Arabia is a shopping mall built as part of the City of Arabia in the Dubailand theme park premises in Dubai. The 10-million square-foot mall contains more than 1,000 retail outlets, a rooftop hotel, waterfront dining and entertainment, a theme park, an earth science museum, and a planetarium. It also contains its own monorail system linked with the Dubai Metro along with a 2-story underground parking garage c

voyage.name: Dragon Mart
voyage.address: Al Awir Rd E44, International City
voyage.content: A mall dedicated to Chinese products.

voyage.name: City Centre Mirdif
voyage.address: Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Rd E311 crossing Al Rebat St, Mirdif community
voyage.content: A large mall with more than 500 stores, over 80 restaurants and cafés and plenty of entertainment and recreation sites inside it.

voyage.name: Dubai Festival City Mall
voyage.content: Has Dubai's only Ikea, since it relocated from City Centre, and a huge Plug-Ins electronic store. Also an ACE Hardware and an amazing mall that has 550 shops.

voyage.name: Cityland Mall
voyage.content: Relatively small mall near Global Village. There tends to be significantly less people here that other malls so expect a more quiet shopping experience.

voyage.name: Al Mallah
voyage.content: Amazing food. It is popular for casual dining, juices, sandwiches and fast food. A good place to visit along with family and friends.

voyage.name: Sidra
voyage.content: Specialized in Arabic, Lebanese and Middle Eastern Foods. This spacious alfresco area is bigger than other restaurants, full of shrubs and bushes with two distinct large indoor spaces - smokers and non-smokers. It is open for post party up to 4am.

voyage.name: InterContinental Dubai Festival City
voyage.content: 498 rooms over 36 floors with views of the Dubai Creek and a 3800-m² event centre. Attached to the Festival Centre shopping mall.

voyage.name: The Meydan Hotel
voyage.address: Meydan Racecourse, Al Meydan Road, Nad Al Sheba
voyage.content: Stylish hotel with 285 furnished rooms. It is equipped with rooftop pool, fitness center, spas, recreations centers like tennis and target shooting games. Its restaurant is specialized in steaks, Italian and Asian cuisine. Ladies-only units are also available.

voyage.name: Hotel ibis
voyage.price: 129 dirham for a room with a double bed
voyage.content: Located on Sheikh Zayed Road, next to Ski Dubai & Mall of the Emirates. This mid-range hotel has 204 cozy air-conditioned with bathtubs. Equipped with Italian restaurant, coffee shop and bar. Private indoor parking available.

voyage.name: Studio One
voyage.price: 151 dirham per night for a single room, however can be up to 900 depending on time of year
voyage.content: A hotel in Studio City with many great restaurants (including Italian, Mexican, and Irish cuisine). The rooms are filled with modern art-y decor, as is the lobby. It also has a pool.

voyage.name: Dubai Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Clean budget hotel that offers private double rooms with comfortable beds with air conditioning. Equipped with swimming pool and good food restaurant.
